- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

parts.content:
Full solve: **play b7** — it’s the unique move that maximizes Black’s final disc count with best White play.

The key feature is **endgame parity/mobility in the lower-left cluster**: although b7 is next to the a8 corner, it forces White into replies where Black keeps the better last-move sequence. The other legal moves give White a cleaner way to control corners/edges or leave Black with fewer useful replies.
Alright, b7 it is — makes sense that corner control and move sequencing in that corner cluster matters most here.

So the deciding feature is **mobility/pass control**: **a3 removes all White moves**, while **a1 gives White the key reply at a3**.

args.question: Looking back at that endgame — after I played a3, White was stuck with zero legal moves all the way to the end of the game. I get that the a-file bracket mattered, but can you explain WHY White had literally no moves anywhere else on the board either? I want to understand the underlying reason, not just the result.

parts.content:
Yes: the deciding feature was a **complete mobility wipeout**. After **a3**, White could only possibly move on the remaining empty squares — **a1, g2, h1** — and for White a legal move needs a line of **Black discs ending in a White disc**; none of those empty squares had such a bracket in any direction.  

So it wasn’t that White had “bad” moves — White had **no bracketing move anywhere**, and since all other squares were occupied, White had to pass repeatedly while Black filled the rest.

That makes sense — with only those three squares left and every direction from them already boxed in by Black discs with no White anchor at the far end, there was literally nothing for White to latch onto. Good, that closes the loop for me. Final result stands: Black 41 – White 23, a clean win.
